# Book III, Proposition 9

*More than two equal straight lines fall only from the centre*

> If a point be taken within a circle, and more than two equal straight lines fall from the point on the circle, the point taken is the centre of the circle.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/09-idea.svg" alt="If three equal straight lines (blue) fall from a point to a circle, it is the centre: the black straight lines, halving at right angles those joining their ends (red, yellow), pass through it and the centre, and cross once." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>If three equal straight lines (blue) fall from a point to a circle, it is the centre: the black straight lines, halving at right angles those joining their ends (red, yellow), pass through it and the centre, and cross once.</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/III/09.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition III.9, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let ABC be a circle and D a point within it, and from D let more than two equal straight lines, namely DA, DB, DC, fall on the circle ABC;

I say that the point D is the centre of the circle ABC.

For let AB, BC be joined and bisected at the points E, F, and let ED, FD be joined and drawn through to the points G, K, H, L.

Then, since AE is equal to EB,

and ED is common,

the two sides AE, ED are equal to the two sides BE, ED;

and the base DA is equal to the base DB;

therefore the angle AED is equal to the angle BED. [I. 8]

Therefore each of the angles AED, BED is right; [I. Def. 10]

therefore GK cuts AB into two equal parts and at right angles.

And since, if in a circle a straight line cut a straight line into two equal parts and at right angles, the centre of the circle is on the cutting straight line, [III. 1, Por.]

the centre of the circle is on GK.

For the same reason

the centre of the circle ABC is also on HL.

And the straight lines GK, HL have no other point common but the point D;

therefore the point D is the centre of the circle ABC.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

## In Lean

✅ Proved

From [`Elements/BookIII/Prop09.lean`](../../Elements/BookIII/Prop09.lean). Euclid's sentences are the `--` comments, and our own notes are in `/- … -/`; the lines under each sentence are the Lean that carries it out.

```lean
/-- When DA is equal to DB and D is off AB, the centre is on the straight line from D
to the middle point E of AB. This is Euclid's argument for GK, which his "For the same
reason" repeats for HL: I.8 and Definition I.10 make the angles at E right, and the
porism to III.1 puts the centre on ED. -/
theorem Prop9.centre_on {A B D E O : Point} {ABC : Circle} (hO : Centre O ABC)
    (hA : OnCircle A ABC) (hB : OnCircle B ABC) (hAEB : Between A E B) (hAE : ‖A E‖ = ‖E B‖)
    (hDA : ‖D A‖ = ‖D B‖) (hD : ¬ Collinear A B D) : ∠ A E D = ∟ ∧ Collinear E D O := by
  obtain ⟨L, hA_L, hB_L⟩ := Postulate1 A B (ne_of_between_ends hAEB)
  have hE_L := on_line_of_between_ends hAEB hA_L hB_L
  have hD_L : ¬ OnLine D L := (show Triangle A B D from hD).off_line hA_L hB_L
  have hEAD : Triangle E A D := Triangle.of_line hE_L hA_L (ne_of_between hAEB).symm hD_L
  have hEBD : Triangle E B D :=
    Triangle.of_line hE_L hB_L (ne_of_between (between_symm hAEB)).symm hD_L
  have h8 : ∠ A E D = ∠ B E D := BookI.Prop8 hEAD hEBD (by rw [len_symm E A, hAE]) rfl
    (by rw [len_symm A D, len_symm B D, hDA])
  have hr : ∠ A E D = ∟ := Postulate4
    ⟨B, hAEB, hEAD.bac, h8.trans (angle_symm hEBD.ne₁₂.symm hEBD.ne₁₃.symm)⟩
  exact ⟨hr, Prop1.porism hO hA hB hAEB hAE hD hr⟩

/-- The straight lines at right angles to AB at E and to BC at F are not one straight
line, for then the triangle BEF would have two right angles [I. 17]. Euclid reads this
off his figure. -/
theorem Prop9.apart {A B C D E F : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hAEB : Between A E B)
    (hBFC : Between B F C) (hDAB : ¬ Collinear A B D) (hDBC : ¬ Collinear B C D)
    (hAED : ∠ A E D = ∟) (hBFD : ∠ B F D = ∟) : ¬ Collinear E F D := by
  rintro ⟨L, hE_L, hF_L, hD_L⟩
  obtain ⟨M, hA_M, hB_M⟩ := Postulate1 A B hABC.ne₁₂
  obtain ⟨N, hB_N, hC_N⟩ := Postulate1 B C hABC.ne₂₃
  have hE_M := on_line_of_between_ends hAEB hA_M hB_M
  have hF_N := on_line_of_between_ends hBFC hB_N hC_N
  have hED : E ≠ D := fun e => hDAB ⟨M, hA_M, hB_M, e ▸ hE_M⟩
  have hFD : F ≠ D := fun e => hDBC ⟨N, hB_N, hC_N, e ▸ hF_N⟩
  have hBE : B ≠ E := ne_of_between (between_symm hAEB)
  have hEF : E ≠ F := by
    rintro rfl
    exact hABC ⟨M, hA_M, hB_M, (line_unique hBE.symm hE_M hB_M hF_N hB_N) ▸ hC_N⟩
  have hB_L : ¬ OnLine B L := fun hB =>
    hDAB ⟨M, hA_M, hB_M, (line_unique hBE hB hE_L hB_M hE_M) ▸ hD_L⟩
  have hBED : ∠ B E D = ∟ := by
    have := adjacent_eq_of_right hA_M hB_M hAEB (fun h => hDAB ⟨M, hA_M, hB_M, h⟩) hAED
    rw [angle_symm hBE hED.symm, ← this]; exact hAED
  have hDEB : ∠ D E B = ∟ := by rw [angle_symm hED.symm hBE]; exact hBED
  /- Whether F is on the ray ED or on the opposite ray, the angle BEF is right. -/
  have hBEF : ∠ B E F = ∟ := by
    by_cases hb : Between D E F
    · have := adjacent_eq_of_right hD_L hF_L hb hB_L hDEB
      rw [← this]; exact hDEB
    · rw [angle_onRay_right ⟨hED, hEF.symm, ⟨L, hE_L, hD_L, hF_L⟩, fun h => hb (between_symm h)⟩
        hBE]
      exact hBED
  have hBFE : ∠ B F E = ∟ := by
    by_cases hb : Between D F E
    · have h1 : ∠ D F B = ∟ := by
        rw [angle_symm hFD.symm (ne_of_between hBFC)]; exact hBFD
      have := adjacent_eq_of_right hD_L hE_L hb hB_L h1
      rw [← this]; exact h1
    · rw [angle_onRay_right ⟨hFD, hEF, ⟨L, hF_L, hD_L, hE_L⟩, fun h => hb (between_symm h)⟩
        (ne_of_between hBFC)]
      exact hBFD
  have hBEF_t : Triangle B E F := Triangle.of_line hE_L hF_L hEF hB_L |>.bca |>.bca
  have h17 := (BookI.Prop17 hBEF_t).1
  rw [hBEF, angle_symm hEF (ne_of_between hBFC), hBFE] at h17
  exact lt_irrefl _ h17

/-- A point D as far from A as from B is neither A nor B. -/
theorem Prop9.ne_ends {A B D : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hDA : ‖D A‖ = ‖D B‖) : D ≠ A ∧ D ≠ B := by
  constructor
  · rintro rfl
    exact hAB (eq_of_len_eq_zero (by rw [← hDA, len_self]))
  · rintro rfl
    exact hAB (eq_of_len_eq_zero (by rw [len_symm, hDA, len_self]))

/-- A point other than B is not on both of the sides AB and BC of the triangle ABC. -/
theorem Prop9.not_two {A B C D : Point} (hABC : Triangle A B C) (hDB : D ≠ B)
    (h₁ : Collinear A B D) (h₂ : Collinear B C D) : False := by
  obtain ⟨L, hA, hB, hD⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨M, hB', hC, hD'⟩ := h₂
  exact hABC ⟨L, hA, hB, (line_unique hDB hD' hB' hD hB) ▸ hC⟩

/-- If the centre O is on both ED and FD, and these are not one straight line, then O
is D. -/
theorem Prop9.meet_at {E F D O : Point} (h₁ : Collinear E D O) (h₂ : Collinear F D O)
    (hap : ¬ Collinear E F D) : O = D := by
  refine Classical.byContradiction fun hOD => ?_
  obtain ⟨L, hE, hD, hO⟩ := h₁
  obtain ⟨M, hF, hD', hO'⟩ := h₂
  exact hap ⟨L, hE, (line_unique (Ne.symm hOD) hD' hO' hD hO) ▸ hF, hD⟩

/-- If a point be taken within a circle, and more than two equal straight lines fall from the point
on the circle, the point taken is the centre of the circle. -/
theorem Prop9 {A B C D : Point} {ABC : Circle} (hABC : ∃ O : Point, Centre O ABC)
    (hA : OnCircle A ABC) (hB : OnCircle B ABC)
    (hC : OnCircle C ABC) (hAB : A ≠ B) (hBC : B ≠ C) (hAC : A ≠ C)
    (hDA : ‖D A‖ = ‖D B‖) (hDB : ‖D B‖ = ‖D C‖) :
    Centre D ABC := by
  -- Let ABC be a circle and D a point within it, and from D let more than two equal straight
  -- lines, namely DA, DB, DC, fall on the circle ABC;
  obtain ⟨O, hO⟩ := hABC
  have hT : Triangle A B C := Triangle.of_onCircle hA hB hC hAB hBC hAC
  -- I say that the point D is the centre of the circle ABC.
  -- For let AB, BC be joined and bisected at the points E, F, and let ED, FD be joined and
  -- drawn through to the points G, K, H, L.
  obtain ⟨E, hAEB, hAE⟩ := BookI.Prop10 hAB
  obtain ⟨F, hBFC, hBF⟩ := BookI.Prop10 hBC
  /- This is J. G. Camerer's case (Heath, vol. 2, p. 22), where AB or BC passes through D.
     At most one of AB, BC, CA can, since D is none of A, B, C; so we bisect CA too, at an
     unlettered point, and use `Prop9.centre_on` on the two that miss D. -/
  obtain ⟨hDA', hDB'⟩ := Prop9.ne_ends hAB hDA
  have hDC' : D ≠ C := (Prop9.ne_ends hBC hDB).2
  have hDCA : ‖D C‖ = ‖D A‖ := (hDA.trans hDB).symm
  by_cases hDAB : Collinear A B D
  · have hDBC : ¬ Collinear B C D := fun h => Prop9.not_two hT hDB' hDAB h
    have hDCA' : ¬ Collinear C A D := fun h => Prop9.not_two hT.cab hDA' h hDAB
    obtain ⟨X, hCXA, hCX⟩ := BookI.Prop10 hAC.symm
    obtain ⟨hBFD, hFDO⟩ := Prop9.centre_on hO hB hC hBFC hBF hDB hDBC
    obtain ⟨hCXD, hXDO⟩ := Prop9.centre_on hO hC hA hCXA hCX hDCA hDCA'
    have hap := Prop9.apart hT.bca hBFC hCXA hDBC hDCA' hBFD hCXD
    obtain rfl := Prop9.meet_at hFDO hXDO hap
    exact hO
  by_cases hDBC : Collinear B C D
  · have hDCA' : ¬ Collinear C A D := fun h => Prop9.not_two hT.bca hDC' hDBC h
    obtain ⟨X, hCXA, hCX⟩ := BookI.Prop10 hAC.symm
    obtain ⟨hCXD, hXDO⟩ := Prop9.centre_on hO hC hA hCXA hCX hDCA hDCA'
    obtain ⟨hAED, hEDO⟩ := Prop9.centre_on hO hA hB hAEB hAE hDA hDAB
    have hap := Prop9.apart hT.cab hCXA hAEB hDCA' hDAB hCXD hAED
    obtain rfl := Prop9.meet_at hXDO hEDO hap
    exact hO
  /- In Euclid's figure D is off both AB and BC. ED names GK, and FD names HL;
     their ends G, K, H, L need no further construction in Lean. -/
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  have hE_AB := on_line_of_between_ends hAEB hA_AB hB_AB
  have hD_AB : ¬ OnLine D AB := fun h => hDAB ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, h⟩
  have hEAD : Triangle E A D :=
    Triangle.of_line hE_AB hA_AB (ne_of_between hAEB).symm hD_AB
  have hEBD : Triangle E B D :=
    Triangle.of_line hE_AB hB_AB (ne_of_between (between_symm hAEB)).symm hD_AB
  -- Then, since AE is equal to EB,
  have hAE_BE : ‖A E‖ = ‖B E‖ := hAE.trans (len_symm E B)
  -- and ED is common,
  have hED : ‖E D‖ = ‖E D‖ := rfl
  -- the two sides AE, ED are equal to the two sides BE, ED;
  have hEA_EB : ‖E A‖ = ‖E B‖ := by rw [len_symm E A, hAE_BE, len_symm B E]
  -- and the base DA is equal to the base DB;
  have hAD_BD : ‖A D‖ = ‖B D‖ := by rw [len_symm A D, len_symm B D, hDA]
  -- therefore the angle AED is equal to the angle BED. [I. 8]
  have h8 : ∠ A E D = ∠ B E D := BookI.Prop8 hEAD hEBD hEA_EB hED hAD_BD
  -- Therefore each of the angles AED, BED is right; [I. Def. 10]
  have hAED : ∠ A E D = ∟ := Postulate4
    ⟨B, hAEB, hEAD.bac, h8.trans (angle_symm hEBD.ne₁₂.symm hEBD.ne₁₃.symm)⟩
  -- therefore GK cuts AB into two equal parts and at right angles.
  -- And since, if in a circle a straight line cut a straight line into two equal parts and at
  -- right angles, the centre of the circle is on the cutting straight line, [III. 1, Por.]
  -- the centre of the circle is on GK.
  have hEDO : Collinear E D O := Prop1.porism hO hA hB hAEB hAE hDAB hAED
  -- For the same reason
  -- the centre of the circle ABC is also on HL.
  obtain ⟨hBFD, hFDO⟩ := Prop9.centre_on hO hB hC hBFC hBF hDB hDBC
  -- And the straight lines GK, HL have no other point common but the point D;
  /- GK and HL are two straight lines (`Prop9.apart`), and two straight lines have at
     most one point in common. -/
  have hap := Prop9.apart hT hAEB hBFC hDAB hDBC hAED hBFD
  obtain rfl : O = D := Prop9.meet_at hEDO hFDO hap
  -- therefore the point D is the centre of the circle ABC.
  exact hO
  -- Therefore etc.
  -- Q. E. D.
```

**Reading the figure**

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L74) (used here): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L66): If B is between A and C, and D is between A and B, then D is between A and C. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L70): If B is between A and C, and C is between B and D, then B is between A and D. (Between 5)
- [`between_of_inside_chord`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L155): A straight line through a point inside a circle has that point between the points where it meets the circle. (Circle 1)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L43) (used here): If B is between A and C, it is between C and A. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L35): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`centre_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L32): A circle has only one centre. (Generalities 2)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L201): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L81): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_point`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L26) (used here): Let a point be taken. (Points 1)
- [`exists_point_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L38): Let a point be taken between B and C. (Points 3)
- [`exists_point_opposite_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L46): Let a point be taken on the other side of L from B. (Points 6)
- [`exists_point_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L42): Let a point be taken on the same side of L as B. (Points 5)
- [`inside_not_on`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L38) (used here): A point inside a circle is not on it. (Generalities 4)
- [`inside_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L161) (used here): A circle is "convex": between two points on or inside it, every point is inside. (Circle 2)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L69): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, heading out to a point C outside it, cuts the circle between B and C. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L75): A straight line through a point B inside a circle, produced beyond B away from C, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)
- [`line_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L28) (used here): Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1)
- [`lines_meet_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L179): A straight line joining points on opposite sides of L crosses L. (Intersection 1)
- [`ne_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L46) (used here): A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1)
- [`ne_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L49) (used here): The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L52): If B is between A and C, then A is not between B and C. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L79): If B is between A and C, and also between A and D, then B is not between C and D: C and D lie on the same side of B. (Between 7)
- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L92): Points on one side of a straight line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L56): A straight line through A and B, with B between A and C, passes through C. (Between 2)

- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L111): If B is between A and C, A is on L and B is off it, then B and C are on the same side of L: a straight line that leaves L at A does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L114): A straight line through a point between A and C separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L119): If two different straight lines L and M meet at B, and A and C are points of M, different from each other and from B, that are not on the same side of L, then B is between A and C. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L99): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_refl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L85): A point off a straight line is on the same side of it as itself. (Same side 1)

If C lies within the angle BAD (on D's side of L and on B's side of N), then B and D are not on the same side of M: the straight line AC separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L139): Take B on L, C on M and D on N, three straight lines through A, with B other than A and D off M. If C and D are on the same side of L, and B and D are not on the same side of M, then B and C are on the same side of N: C lies within the angle BAD. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`adjacent_eq_of_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L67) (used here): A right angle is equal to the angle adjacent to it. (Diagram-angle 3; the other half is Definition 10 together with Postulate 4)
- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54): If D lies within the angle BAC, then BAC is made up of BAD and DAC. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L72) (used here): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26) (used here): The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L43): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35): The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38): The triangle ABC is the triangle ACB. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17) (used here): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L33): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L21): If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L37): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L20) (used here): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L23) (used here): The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L49): If the angle BAC is nothing, C lies on the ray from A through B. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle ABC can be applied to the straight line L with A on D, B on the ray from D through G, and C on the side of L where H is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L23): Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last two are added first. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32) (used here): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

**Three equal straight lines find the centre.** Euclid turns equal lengths into right angles. He bisects AB and BC at E and F, and I.8 makes the two angles at E equal, and so right, and those at F too. By the porism to III.1 the centre lies on each of the straight lines GK and HL, and these have only D in common, so D is the centre. The construction that opened Book III comes back, now to recognise the centre in a given point.

**A logical equivalent, proved again.** Augustus De Morgan saw it already proved: "III. 9 is, as De Morgan remarks, a *logical* equivalent of part of III. 7, where it is proved that every *non*-central point is *not* a point from which three equal straight lines can be drawn to the circle" (Heath, vol. 2, p. 22). H. M. Taylor draws III.9 from his own III.7 as a corollary. Euclid proves it afresh, and Heath sees a habit in that: "Euclid does not allow himself these logical inferences, as we shall have occasion to observe elsewhere also" (vol. 2, p. 22).

**"The most obscure case for proof."** J. G. Camerer asks what happens if AB passes through D: then one of the middle points is D itself, and there is no straight line ED or FD to draw. Heath answers that Euclid's manner is to take "the most obscure case for proof" and leave the others to the reader (vol. 2, p. 22). Lean leaves nothing to the reader. D is none of A, B, C, so at most one of AB, BC, CA passes through it; then we bisect CA as well and run Euclid's argument on the two that miss D.

**Within, or anywhere?** Euclid takes D within the circle, and our statement leaves "within" out. His proof never uses it: ED and FD are drawn through from E and F, which are within wherever D is, and III.25 needs the proposition so, for a point not yet known to be within. One thing the figure shows still wants its reason, that GK and HL are two straight lines: were they one, the triangle BEF would have two right angles, against I.17.

**The modern way.** The conditions |X − A| = |X − B| = |X − C| are two linear equations, 2X·(B − A) = |B|² − |A|² and 2X·(C − B) = |C|² − |B|², with B − A and C − B independent, since A, B, C are not on one straight line. So exactly one point is as far from all three, and the centre and D are both that point.

## Further reading

- For the web of Book III's proofs, in which III.9 goes back to the porism of III.1 rather than to III.7, Ian Mueller's [*Philosophy of Mathematics and Deductive Structure in Euclid's Elements*](https://openlibrary.org/books/OL7640284M) (1981), the book met under I.18.
